To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) algorithm configuration can be automated, and (ii) this automation leads to substantial improvements in algorithm performance.

(1) The performance of high-quality parameterized algorithms for SAT and MIP can be significantly improved by automatically configuring their parameters, and (2) the best algorithm configuration procedures for this problem are local search-based, combined with adaptive capping.

1) The configuration of discrete algorithm parameters can have an important impact on performance; 2) the configuration of discrete algorithmic parameters is a challenging search problem; 3) local search is a powerful approach to solving this problem; 4) adaptive capping is a powerful method for accelerating local search; and 5) algorithm configuration can yield significant performance gains.

the design of an automatic algorithm configuration system that can be applied to a wide range of parameterized algorithms and that yields significant performance improvements.
the automatic optimization of parameter settings for parameterized algorithms.

The main takeaway from our work is that

algorithm configuration is a viable alternative to hand-tuning for the optimization of parameterized algorithms on a class of problem instances; moreover, the performance of the resulting algorithms is often comparable to that of their best-known hand-tuned versions.
algorithm configuration is a promising direction for the development of high-performance software.

algorithm configuration is not a one-off task that can be done once and for all, but rather a continuous process that must be performed whenever the target problem domain or the algorithms being used change.
